questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used. At temperatures close to 0K, the specific heat capacity c of a particular solid is given by c = bT3, where T is the temperature and b is a constant, characteristic of the solid. The SI unit of specific heat capacity is Jkg–1K–1. What is the unit of constant b, expressed in SI base units?

A digital balance is used to weigh ingredients in a laboratory. When a weight is applied to the digital balance, an electronic circuit generates a current which is then converted into a digital readout on the display. The electronic circuit gives a current of 2.0mA when a weight of 30N is applied, and a current of 0.5mA when a weight of 5N is applied. Which calibration curve could represent this circuit?
Four students measure a time interval that is known to be 1.734s. The measurement recorded by each student is shown. Which measurement is the most accurate?
A mass on the end of a spring bounces up and down as shown, after being released at time t = 0. distance up 0 time t distance down Which graph shows how the velocity varies with time? velocity up

A stone is thrown vertically upwards from a point that is 12m above the sea. It then falls into the sea below after 3.4s. Air resistance is negligible. At which speed was the stone released when it was thrown?
Two balls X and Y are moving towards each other with speeds of 5ms–1 and 15ms–1 respectively.

In the absence of air resistance, a ball thrown horizontally from a tower with velocity v, will land after time T seconds. If, however, air resistance is taken into account, which statement is correct?

options.A: The ball lands with a horizontal velocity less than v after more than T seconds.
options.B: The ball lands with a horizontal velocity less than v after T seconds.
options.C: The ball lands with a horizontal velocity v after more than T seconds.
options.D: The ball lands with a horizontal velocity v after T seconds.

questions.questionText: Two balls, of masses m and 2m, travelling in a vacuum with initial velocities 2v and v respectively, collide with each other head-on, as shown. m 2v v 2m After the collision, the ball of mass m rebounds to the left with velocity v. What is the loss of kinetic energy in the collision?

options.A: 3 mv2 B 3 mv2 C 9 mv2 D 9 mv2

questions.questionText: A ball falls through a liquid at a constant speed. It is acted upon by three forces: an upthrust, a drag-force and its weight. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The drag-force increases with increasing depth.
options.B: The drag-force is equal to the sum of the upthrust and weight.
options.C: The upthrust is constant with increasing depth.
options.D: The weight is greater than the sum of the drag-force and the upthrust.

A uniform horizontal beam OX, 4.0m long and weighing 100N, is hinged at a wall at point O. It is supported by a cord XY which is attached to the wall at Y. Y cord O 30° X 4.0 m What is the tension in the cord?

An object shaped as a hemisphere rests with its flat surface on a table. The object has radius r and density ρ. r table The volume of a sphere is 4 πr3. Which average pressure does the object exert on the table?
Which statement best represents the principle of conservation of energy?

options.A: Energy cannot be used faster than it is created.
options.B: The supply of energy is limited, so energy must be conserved.
options.C: The total energy in a closed system is constant.
options.D: The total energy input to a system is equal to the useful energy output.

questions.questionText: A crane is being used to lift containers off a ship. One container has a mass of 14000kg and is being lifted vertically with a speed of 3.2ms–1. The electric motor being used to supply the power to lift the container is using a current of 240A at a potential difference of 2200V. What is the efficiency of the system?

Leonardo da Vinci proposed a flying machine that would work like a screw to lift the pilot into the air. The ‘screw’ is rotated by the pilot. The machine and the pilot together have a total mass of 120kg. Which useful output power must the pilot provide to move vertically upwards at a constant speed of 2.5ms–1?

A metal wire, fixed at one end, has length l and cross-sectional area A. The wire extends a distance e when mass m is hung from the other end of the wire. What is an expression for the Young Modulus E of the metal? ml mgl me mge

A sound wave passes through air. The diagram shows the positions of the molecules of the air at one instant. P Q R S Which distance is equal to the wavelength of the wave?

options.A: PQ B PS C QR D QS

questions.questionText: The top row of bars represents a set of particles inside the Earth and at rest. The lower row represents the same particles at one instant as a longitudinal wave passes from left to right through the Earth. What should be measured to determine the amplitude of the oscillations of the particles in the lower row as the wave passes?

options.A: half the maximum displacement of the particles from their position at rest
options.B: half the maximum distance apart of the particles
options.C: the maximum displacement of the particles from their position at rest
options.D: the maximum distance apart of the particles

questions.questionText: A straight tube is closed at one end and has a loudspeaker positioned at the open end. The frequency of the loudspeaker is initially very low and is increased slowly. A series of loudness maxima are heard. The stationary wave which gives the first maximum has a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end. The frequency of the loudspeaker is f when the first maximum is heard. What is the frequency of the loudspeaker when the fourth maximum is heard? 7f

A buzzer emitting sound of frequency 846Hz is attached to a string and rotated in a horizontal circle. The linear speed of the buzzer is 25.0ms–1. buzzer observer The speed of sound is 340ms–1. What is the maximum frequency heard by the observer?

The diagram shows the principal regions of the electromagnetic spectrum, with some details labelled. The diagram is not to scale. Q 10–10 m wavelength increasing What is a typical order of magnitude of the wavelength of the radiation in region Q?

A transverse stationary wave of constant maximum amplitude is formed on the string. x x P S R T Q P, R and Q are the only points on the string where nodes are formed.
